properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive dependency of the ERC-1155 dapp's JS stack (pulled via elliptic, the secp256k1 ECDSA engine used by hdkey/ethereumjs-util). hash.js ships SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512, HMAC and RIPEMD160 implementations. No direct hash.js call site in first-party code (scripts/migrations do no hashing themselves), but the algorithms ship with the dependency tree regardless. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability, not use — no 3DES call site in app.py. The pin is 2017-vintage. NOTE (file-level coverage): metadata-api/requirements.txt also declares the Ethereum secp256k1 ECDSA signing stack that report_finding folds into this object's file — bitcoin==1.1.42 (line 6, pybitcointools), coincurve==6.0.0 (line 12), ethereum==1.6.1 (line 17), pysha3==1.0.2 (line 49, Keccak-256), secp256k1==0.13.2 (line 58), web3==3.11.0 (line 71). All Shor-vulnerable signing capability shipped in the API environmen

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 ships with crypto-js 3.3.0 (alongside SHA-1/SHA-2/AES/HMAC/DES), a transitive dep of the web3/opensea-js/0x subprovider stack. No CryptoJS.* call site in first-party code (grep found zero), so no active MD5 use — capability present in the shipped dependency tree. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 ships with crypto-js 3.3.0 in the JS dependency tree. No first-party call site (grep CryptoJS = 0 hits in the whole repo), so it is an available-but-unused algorithm of a declared dependency; collision-broken SHA-1 would matter only if the wallet stack ever calls it (ethereumjs code paths hash with keccak256, not SHA-1). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: No RSA call site in app.py; the live RSA use in this service is Google service-account RS256 JWT signing driven from app.py:151 (filed as a separate finding). Both pins are 2017-vintage.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA1 applies to any Flask session cookie / signed token this API issues; changeable here by pinning itsdangerous>=1.1 (SHA-512-based default) alongside a Flask upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: No Ed25519 call site in project scripts — availability in the shipped dependency graph, not app use. tweetnacl 0.13.2 predates the 0.14+ security releases.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is not just declared, it is the live signature primitive of the dapp's wallet path: @0x/subproviders MnemonicWalletSubprovider (scripts/sell.js:29, scripts/initial_sale.js:32) and truffle-hdwallet-provider (truffle-config.js:51,59) derive BIP32 keys (hdkey/ethereumjs-wallet) and sign Ethereum transactions and Wyvern orders with elliptic's secp256k1 ECDSA. Quantum-vulnerable (Shor) signing on a production code path. Changeable here (migrate on schedule to ML-DSA-style signing once Ethereum i

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic also implements ECDH key agreement (the same library object as the ECDSA finding). Ethereum's key use in this codebase is signature-only; no ECDH call site exists in first-party code. The capability ships with the declared dependency, and any future key-agreement feature would reach it. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 (nacl.box scalarmult) ships with tweetnacl, which is declared in three version ranges in the JS dependency tree. No nacl/tweetnacl call site in first-party code (grep found zero), so this is available-in-shipped-library, not active use. The dapp's actual key exchange is TLS to Infura (reported separately). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt is genuinely declared twice — the Python scrypt==0.8.0 package (metadata-api/requirements.txt:57) and scrypt-js 2.0.3/2.0.4 in the JS tree (yarn.lock:7431,7436, used by ethereumjs-wallet for keystore files) — but the 'via Werkzeug' half of the attribution is wrong: Werkzeug 0.12.2's werkzeug.security provides PBKDF2 only; its scrypt method arrived in Werkzeug 2.3. scrypt itself is a memory-hard, quantum-safe password KDF; no direct call site in first-party code (app.py has no password han

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Symmetric — Grover-halved only, no Shor exposure; AES-128 keeps a 64-bit quantum margin while CNSA 2.0 asks for AES-256. Both pins are 2017-vintage with later CVE fixes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Password KDF available in both stacks; no PBKDF2 call site in app.py. The environment also pins memory-hard scrypt on both sides (requirements.txt:57, scrypt-js).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl's secretbox = XSalsa20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption, declared in the JS dependency tree (three version ranges). No nacl call site in first-party code (grep zero hits) — available-in-shipped-library, not active use. The primitive itself is modern and PQ-tolerant (no Shor exposure; Grover only halves the 256-bit key). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the metadata-api's outbound TLS posture: requests 2.18.4 (July 2017) over urllib3 1.22 — a pre-TLS-1.3 stack with ECDHE/RSA key exchange only, no post-quantum group anywhere, and a 2017 certifi trust bundle. The Google Cloud Storage upload path in app.py reaches this stack (google-cloud-storage → google-auth → requests/urllib3 transport); any HTTPS it opens is harvest-now-decrypt-later exposed. Also note aiohttp==2.2.5 (requirements.txt:2) is a second declared TLS-capable HTTP client wit

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The July-2017 bundle is 7+ years stale — roots added since (ISRG, GTS) are absent; trust-store rotation via a certifi upgrade is the changeable part.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ships Ed25519/X25519/XSalsa20-Poly1305 into the build; no direct call site in project scripts. 0.13.2 is a 2017 release superseded by security fixes; upgrade is changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the metadata-api environment; no call site in app.py. Part of the 2017 Ethereum toolchain stack pinned in this requirements file.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same artifact as the CA-trust-bundle object (linked); anchors HTTPS for the requests/urllib3/google-cloud clients in this API.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: 2017 vintage: pre-TLS-1.3, carries known certificate-verification CVEs (CVE-2019-11324, CVE-2018-20060); no post-quantum key exchange possible at this version.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pycryptodome 3.4.7 (2018) ships AES, DES/3DES, Blowfish, RSA, SHA, MD5, HMAC — the Python-side 3DES and other ALG objects in this inventory trace to this pin. No Crypto/Cryptodome import exists in app.py (the only first-party Python module), so no call site is found; the algorithms ship with the declared dependency regardless. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js is the transitive dep through which MD5/SHA-1/AES/HMAC (separate ALG objects) reach the build. No CryptoJS.* call site in first-party code (grep zero hits across the repo); its role here is declared-capability of the web3/opensea-js/0x dependency tree. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The JS memory-hard KDF used for BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed derivation inside the Ethereum wallet path; no direct call site in project scripts (reached transitively via @0x/subproviders).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-2 hashing available to the JS build inside the transaction-signing stack; no direct call site in project scripts.

properties.value: That release signs tokens with SHA-1-derived HMAC by default — see the HMAC-SHA1 algorithm object; the upgrade pin is the fix. No signed-token call site in app.py itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: 2017 TLS defaults with no post-quantum key exchange; the google-cloud-storage uploads driven from app.py ride this stack via urllib3/certifi.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This pin has a live indirect consumer: google-auth==1.4.1 (requirements.txt:22) uses the python rsa package to sign RS256 (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5, SHA-256) service-account JWTs for Google Cloud Storage — app.py loads credentials via service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_file() on every image upload. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Werkzeug 0.12.2 is Flask's WSGI toolkit; its crypto surface is werkzeug.security PBKDF2 password hashing and (with itsdangerous==0.24, requirements.txt:31) signed cookies. app.py sets no secret_key, defines no sessions and does no password handling, so no call site exists in first-party code — the capability ships with the dep. A 2017 pin (known CVEs in later Werkzeug releases make the version itself worth tracking). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Provides the SHA-2/RIPEMD-160 hashing used inside the JS secp256k1 address-derivation stack (elliptic 6.x); no direct call site in project scripts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This JS PBKDF2 is transitively live: bip39@2.5.0/^2.5.0 (yarn.lock:1560,1571) uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with 2048 iterations to derive the wallet seed from the BIP39 mnemonic — the first step of MnemonicWalletSubprovider/truffle-hdwallet-provider key derivation (scripts/sell.js:29, truffle-config.js:51). PBKDF2 itself is quantum-safe; the finding is the declared capability on a live wallet path. Changeable here.
